title: The Hadwiger–Finsler Inequality (Sharpening of Weitzenböck)
description: For any triangle with side lengths a, b, c and area T, a² + b² + c² ≥ 4·√3·T + (a−b)² + (b−c)² + (c−a)², with equality iff the triangle is equilateral. This is the canonical strengthening of Weitzenböck's inequality: the extra term (a−b)²+(b−c)²+(c−a)² ≥ 0 quantifies the slack in the Weitzenböck bound, so dropping it recovers the parent. Proved by reducing to L := 2(ab+bc+ca)−(a²+b²+c²) ≥ 4√3·T, squaring to L² ≥ 48T², and discharging the unconditional Ravi-substitution SOS identity L² − 48T² = ½((pq−qr)²+(qr−rp)²+(rp−pq)²) with p=b+c−a, q=c+a−b, r=a+b−c.

The area is supplied via Heron's squared identity 16T² = 2a²b²+2b²c²+2c²a²−a⁴−b⁴−c⁴ and the triangle inequalities a ≤ b+c, b ≤ c+a, c ≤ a+b are taken as hypotheses (they are precisely what is needed for L ≥ 0). overview.historicalContext: The Hadwiger–Finsler inequality, published by Paul Finsler and Hugo Hadwiger in 1937, sharpens Weitzenböck's 1919 inequality a²+b²+c² ≥ 4√3·T by adding the nonnegative correction term (a−b)²+(b−c)²+(c−a)². It is tight precisely for the equilateral triangle and sits at the base of a hierarchy of refined triangle inequalities. The cleanest proof uses the Ravi substitution a = q+r, b = r+p, c = p+q (equivalently p = b+c−a, etc.), under which both the area and the sides become symmetric in p, q, r and the inequality collapses to a classical symmetric SOS fact. This is the route formalized here, building directly on the parent Weitzenböck formalization whose recorded open question was exactly this strengthening.
overview.problemStatement: For a triangle with side lengths a, b, c > 0 satisfying the triangle inequalities and area T, prove a² + b² + c² ≥ 4√3·T + (a−b)² + (b−c)² + (c−a)², with equality iff a = b = c.
overview.proofStrategy:
1. Encode the area through Heron's identity in squared form: 16T² = 2a²b² + 2b²c² + 2c²a² − a⁴ − b⁴ − c⁴.
2. Set L := 2(ab+bc+ca) − (a²+b²+c²). The algebraic identity (a²+b²+c²) − [(a−b)²+(b−c)²+(c−a)²] = L reduces the target to L ≥ 4√3·T.
3. Square the target. It suffices to show L² ≥ (4√3·T)² = 48T².
4. Via the Ravi substitution p = b+c−a, q = c+a−b, r = a+b−c, one has L = pq+qr+rp and 48T² = 3·16T² = 3(p+q+r)pqr, so L² − 48T² = ½((pq−qr)²+(qr−rp)²+(rp−pq)²) ≥ 0 — an unconditional polynomial identity dispatched by nlinarith.
5. Recover the linear inequality: the triangle inequalities give p, q, r ≥ 0, hence L = pq+qr+rp ≥ 0, so √(L²) = L; combine with Real.sqrt_sq and Real.sqrt_le_sqrt.
6. Equality case: tightness forces the SOS to vanish, i.e. pq = qr = rp; with positive sides this forces p = q = r, i.e. a = b = c.
keyInsights: The Finsler excess (a−b)²+(b−c)²+(c−a)² is exactly a²+b²+c² minus L = 2(ab+bc+ca)−(a²+b²+c²), so the whole refinement is a single linear identity away from the parent.
The Ravi substitution makes the squared inequality unconditional: L² − 48T² = ½Σ(pq−qr)² holds for all reals p, q, r, so no triangle hypothesis is needed for the squared form.
Triangle inequalities are needed only to give L ≥ 0 (so |L| = L when un-squaring) — the proof cleanly separates the algebraic content from the geometric admissibility condition.
Hadwiger–Finsler ⟹ Weitzenböck is just dropping the nonnegative excess term, formalized as weitzenbock_of_hadwiger.
The very SOS that proves the inequality pins down its equality case: vanishing forces pq = qr = rp, hence p = q = r, hence the equilateral triangle.

Ravi substitution p = b+c−a, q = c+a−b, r = a+b−c
Sum-of-squares (nonnegativity of squares) and the symmetric inequality (pq+qr+rp)² ≥ 3pqr(p+q+r)

crossReferences.description: Hadwiger–Finsler adds the nonnegative term (a−b)²+(b−c)²+(c−a)² to the right-hand side of Weitzenböck's inequality; weitzenbock_of_hadwiger derives the parent from this entry.
Heron's formula supplies the area expression 16T² = 2a²b²+2b²c²+2c²a²−a⁴−b⁴−c⁴ that this proof takes as the algebraic definition of the squared area.

conclusion.summary: The Hadwiger–Finsler inequality a²+b²+c² ≥ 4√3·T + (a−b)²+(b−c)²+(c−a)² is reduced to L ≥ 4√3·T for L = 2(ab+bc+ca)−(a²+b²+c²), then to the unconditional Ravi-substitution SOS identity L² − 48T² = ½((pq−qr)²+(qr−rp)²+(rp−pq)²). The triangle inequalities enter only to give L ≥ 0, and the equality case (equilateral) falls out of the vanishing of the same SOS.
conclusion.implications: This formalization answers the open question recorded by the parent Weitzenböck entry and machine-checks the refinement relationship Hadwiger–Finsler ⟹ Weitzenböck. Methodologically it shows how the Ravi substitution converts a triangle inequality into a symmetric polynomial inequality where the area and sides are on equal footing, separating the purely algebraic SOS content (true for all reals) from the geometric admissibility condition (triangle inequalities, used only for sign control). The same square-then-discharge-then-unsquare pattern as the parent applies, now with a sharper residue.
openQuestions: Higher refinements in the triangle-inequality hierarchy

sections.title: Equality Characterization
sections.summary: hadwiger_finsler_eq_iff: for positive sides, equality holds iff a = b = c. The vanishing SOS forces the three Ravi differences to zero; positivity then forces p = q = r, hence a = b = c. The reverse direction computes T = √3·a²/4.
